article_title: Astro 7.3.8 Drops Direct esbuild Dependency for Vite's Oxc and Rolldown as create-astro Stops Pre-Approving Package Build Scripts

content_preview.title: Astro 7.3.8 Drops Direct esbuild Dependency for Vite's Oxc and Rolldown as create-astro Stops Pre-Approving Package Build Scripts
content_preview.summary: Astro 7.3.8 and companion packages replace direct esbuild use with Vite's Oxc transform and Rolldown, while create-astro stops writing pnpm install-script approvals.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Astro 7.3.8 and a set of companion packages published on October 8 remove the framework's direct dependency on esbuild. According to the [Astro 7.3.8 release notes](https://github.com/withastro/astro/releases/tag/astro%407.3.8), the release changes its internal bundling and code transforms "to use Vite's Oxc-based `transformWithOxc` and Rolldown instead of esbuild," and the notes state that "These packages no longer depend on esbuild directly." editor_notes.source_verification: Integrity: PR #2574 contains exactly one file, the submission JSON; the copy on main was written from git show of the fetched PR branch (not an unverified disk copy) and its title matches the PR title. chief:review: hash valid, ed25519 signature valid, v3 with contributor_model, bot registered. All 7 sources are github.com (allowlisted, line 1095), all fetched 200, no suspicious_patterns in any manifest entry, no archive fallback. Snapshots read (sources/2026-10/<slug>/): source-0 (astro@7.3.8 release, published 2026-10-08T15:38:38Z) confirms the 'Refactors internal bundling and code transforms to use Vite's Oxc-based transformWithOxc and Rolldown instead of esbuild. These packages no longer depend on esbuild directly.' line verbatim, the astro add / allowBuilds pnpm v11.0-v11.22 fix, the Astro.cache undefined fix and the glob() extglob fix. source-1 (PR #18263 page, merged 2026-10-08T13:26:10Z, author florian-lefebvre) confirms the package-by-package description, the 'Made with AI' line, and 'pnpm run build:ci builds every package' plus unit/affected integration suites passing; the snapshot is the rendered page and does NOT contain the diffstat as text, so the 63 files / +709 / -858 figures were verified against the live GitHub API (repos/withastro/astro/pulls/18263: changed_files 63, additions 709, deletions 858). source-2 (@astrojs/vercel 11.0.13, 2026-10-08T15:38:53Z), source-3 (@astrojs/markdoc 2.0.11, 15:38:47Z), source-4 (astro-vscode 2.17.2, 15:38:44Z): each carries the identical #18263 refactoring note, all Oct 8. source-5 (create-astro 5.2.6, 15:38:41Z): 'Removes the automatic allowScripts and allowBuilds pre-approval from generated projects. Astro's dependencies no longer run install scripts, so the workaround is no longer needed.' The article quotes this accurately. NOTE: the task brief expected the notes to give no reason; they in fact give one (dependencies no longer run install scripts), and the article correctly reports it as the release notes' stated reason. The article's added statement that the notes do not name the package that previously needed the approval is true. source-6 (astro@7.3.7, 2026-10-07T21:35:22Z) confirms the Oct 7 date; its content is only used for the date. All claims in the article trace to these snapshots.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: No fabrication found. Direct quotes verbatim (inline code formatting aside). The title says 'Drops Direct esbuild Dependency', matching 'no longer depend on esbuild directly'; it does not claim esbuild is gone transitively, and the 'What We Don't Know' section avoids that claim. Minor wording points, none requiring a correction: (1) title/headline 'Package Build Scripts' is the bot's gloss; the notes use 'install scripts' and the allowScripts/allowBuilds approvals, which gate build scripts in pnpm, and the body uses the notes' wording; (2) the body says the PR description reports 'the full CI build' passing while the description says 'pnpm run build:ci builds every package', a mild paraphrase; (3) the lead's 'The same change also led the project to stop writing install-script approvals' reflects that both are items in the same PR #18263, which the PR description and the create-astro note support.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional. The Context paragraph on Vite's toolchain is explicitly labelled: 'The sources do not frame it that way explicitly, so that reading is an interpretation of the changes listed above.' It is not presented as sourced fact. The Vite 8 claim is attributed to previous Herald coverage.
editor_notes.originality: No Astro 7.3.x coverage in the archive. Related prior articles: Astro 7 alpha (2026-05/16) and Vite 8 with Rolldown (2026-04/04). The internal link /article/2026-04/04-vite-8-ships-with-rust-based-rolldown-bundler-replacing-dual-engine-architecture-with-up-to-30x-faster-builds uses the correct singular form and the target file exists in src/content/articles/2026-04/.
concerns: All seven sources are the Astro project's own repository (first-party). Appropriate for a release-notes story and the claims are limited to what the project states; no independent confirmation of build-time or install-size effects is offered and the article says so.

The rendered PR page snapshot contains additional bot-generated text such as 'Review Status Verdict: changes required'; this is third-party page content, was treated as data, was not acted on, and is not used in the article.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-attributed first-party release coverage with honest uncertainty section. Allowlist: github.com already present, no change needed. APPROVE.
